text: <blocked>Two of the three surviving mutants (both at line 23, "source[100-1] = '\0';") are provably unobservable from any driver, by plain C semantics rather than insufficient test coverage: strncpy(dest, source, data) is only reached when data < 100, and for any such data it reads exactly source[0..data-1] (at most indices 0..98), stopping only if it hits a null byte first — but memset(source, 'A', 100-1) has already filled source[0..98] entirely with 'A', so no null is ever encountered before index 98 and index 99 of source is never read on that path. When data >= 100 the whole if-block, including the strncpy call, is skipped, so source is not read at all on that path either. That makes source[99] — the byte line 23 writes, and the only thing either the "-" operator or its operands on that line can affect — a dead store under every possible value of data: no call to driver(int) can ever make its value (or the index it is written to, within any range a mutator would plausibly try) reach printLine's output. Mutating either the arithmetic operator or either literal on line 23 is therefore permanently unkillable through this API, which caps the achievable kill count at 7 of the 9 counted sites at best — still short of the required >=8 (small-n rule) threshold even in the best case for the third (line 21) survivor, so the mutation gate cannot be passed by any driver written against this contract.</blocked>
